_meta.title: The Debt & The Plumbing — figures
_meta.units: Dollar amounts are in billions of USD unless a figure's `unit` says otherwise. Rates are percent per year.

status_legend.primary: The number appears in the named primary document (Treasury, Fed, CBO, SEC, GAO). Read from a search excerpt of that document, not from the document opened directly. See `access_note`.
status_legend.secondary: Taken from a secondary site (aggregator, news, research note) that cites the primary source. Must be checked against the primary before publishing.
status_legend.derived: Computed in this file from other figures. The `formula` field shows how.
status_legend.modeled: An approximation built by a script in /scripts. Not a published number.
status_legend.recall: A well-known historical figure entered from memory. Needs checking against the source.

_meta.access_note: On 2026-11-03 the session's network policy blocked direct access to api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov, fiscaldata.treasury.gov, www.federalreserve.gov, markets.newyorkfed.org and fred.stlouisfed.org. Every figure was gathered through web-search excerpts. `scripts/refresh.mjs` pulls the same series straight from the primary APIs once those hosts are allowed.

totalPublicDebt.label: Total public debt outstanding (gross)
totalPublicDebt.source: Treasury, Monthly Statement of the Public Debt (MSPD), Sep 2026, Table I

debtHeldByPublic.label: Debt held by the public
debtHeldByPublic.note: Includes the Federal Reserve's holdings. The Fed counts as 'the public' in Treasury accounting.

intragovernmental.label: Intragovernmental holdings (trust funds etc.)
intragovernmental.note: Mostly non-marketable Government Account Series securities held by Social Security, Medicare, federal pension and other trust funds.

totalPublicDebtLatest.label: Total public debt outstanding, latest daily
totalPublicDebtLatest.source: Treasury, Debt to the Penny (via IndexBox excerpt)

totalPublicDebtOct16.label: Total public debt outstanding
totalPublicDebtOct16.source: Treasury, Debt to the Penny (via fedpolicy.org excerpt)
totalPublicDebtOct16.note: Used with the Oct 29 figure to set the counter's growth rate.

dailyGrowthEstimate.label: Recent average daily increase in gross debt (estimate)
dailyGrowthEstimate.note: Daily debt moves in steps, not smoothly: big jumps on settlement days, small dips on others. Use only for a labeled 'estimate' ticker. The Sep 30 → Oct 29 window gives (40593.6 - 40171.8)/29 ≈ 14.5 bn/day.

marketableTotal.label: Total marketable debt
marketableTotal.source: Treasury, MSPD Sep 2026 (short-term 7,12x + long-term 24,72x per excerpt)
marketableTotal.note: User's starting figure 31.835T matches the excerpt's short-term ≈7.12T + long-term ≈24.72T. Exact million-level figure still to be read off Table I.

nonMarketableTotal.label: Total non-marketable debt
nonMarketableTotal.note: Mostly Government Account Series (trust funds), plus savings bonds, State and Local Government Series (SLGS) and small foreign/other series.

debtLimit.label: Statutory debt limit
debtLimit.source: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) raised the limit by $5T; CRFB debt-ceiling Q&A

debtSubjectToLimit.label: Debt subject to limit
debtSubjectToLimit.source: Treasury, Debt to the Penny / DTS Table III-C (via tensorust.com excerpt)
debtSubjectToLimit.note: Slightly below total public debt because some debt (e.g. unamortized discount, Federal Financing Bank) is excluded. Headroom ≈ $860bn. NTU projects the limit is reached around May 2027; CRFB says mid-to-late 2027.

composition._note: Marketable debt by instrument, Sep 30 2026. Dollar amounts for bills, notes and bonds come from the JEC Monthly Debt Update (citing MSPD). TIPS and FRN dollar amounts are derived from Pier20 percentage shares × marketable total. Average rates come from Treasury's Average Interest Rates dataset (via secondary excerpts).

bills.label: Bills
bills.source: MSPD Sep 2026 via JEC Monthly Debt Update; rate: Treasury Average Interest Rates (via businessquant/tftc excerpts)
bills.note: Share = 7,118 / 31,835. JEC quotes 21.95% because it divides by debt held by the public (32.43T), not marketable debt. Pier20 gives 22.4%.

notes.label: Notes (2–10y)
notes.source: MSPD Sep 2026 via JEC Monthly Debt Update

bonds.label: Bonds (20–30y)
bonds.source: MSPD Sep 2026 via JEC Monthly Debt Update

tips.label: TIPS
tips.note: TIPS average rate is the real coupon. Treasury also pays the inflation adjustment to principal, which this rate leaves out.

check.note: ≈$19bn gap: rounding plus Federal Financing Bank securities. Close once exact Table I values are read.

avgRateMarketable.label: Average interest rate, marketable debt
avgRateMarketable.source: Treasury, Average Interest Rates on U.S. Treasury Securities (via businessquant.com, dollarliquidity.com excerpts)

avgRateAllInterestBearing.label: Average interest rate, all interest-bearing debt
avgRateAllInterestBearing.source: Treasury, Average Interest Rates (via secondary excerpt)

avgRateMarketable2022.label: Average interest rate, marketable debt, early 2022
avgRateMarketable2022.note: Low point of the series was about 1.5–1.6% in early 2022. Confirm the exact month and value.

weightedAvgMaturity.label: Weighted average maturity of marketable debt
weightedAvgMaturity.source: JEC Monthly Debt Update; GAO-26-107529 gives 71 months for Sep 2025

shareMaturingWithin12m.label: Share of marketable debt maturing within 12 months
shareMaturingWithin12m.note: Conference Board gives about 33% for Q3 FY2026 as well. Up from 24% in Sep 2014.

couponsMaturingNext12m.label: Fixed-rate notes & bonds maturing Oct 2026 – Sep 2027
couponsMaturingNext12m.note: Plus $575.8bn of TIPS and FRNs in the same window. Used as the check on the modeled maturity schedule.

deficitFY2026.label: Federal deficit, FY2026
deficitFY2026.source: Treasury, Final Monthly Treasury Statement FY2026

netInterestFY2026.label: Net interest outlays, FY2026
netInterestFY2026.source: Treasury, Final MTS FY2026 (Net Outlays table)
netInterestFY2026.note: Net = gross interest on Treasury debt minus interest received by trust funds and other interest income. FY2025 was about $970bn.

grossInterestFY2026.label: Gross interest expense on Treasury debt, FY2026
grossInterestFY2026.source: Treasury figure reported via ChainCatcher / Yahoo Finance
grossInterestFY2026.note: Gross includes interest paid to trust funds, which is the government paying itself. The user's '$1.17T in 10 months' is consistent with this but unconfirmed.

netInterestShareOutlays.label: Net interest as share of total outlays, FY2026

cboNetInterest.label: CBO projected net interest
cboNetInterest.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036 (Feb 2026)
cboNetInterest.note: Share of outlays: 13.9% (2026) → 18.8% (2036), derived. CBO: rising average interest rates account for about half the increase.

fed._note: H.4.1 release of Oct 29 2026 (Wednesday level, Oct 28). These numbers set the starting state for the balance-sheet identity in the flow map.

totalAssets.label: Fed total assets
totalAssets.source: Federal Reserve H.4.1, Oct 29 2026 (via Trading Economics excerpt)

somaTreasuries.label: SOMA Treasury holdings (bills + notes/bonds + TIPS)
somaTreasuries.source: NY Fed SOMA holdings (via Apify / CEIC excerpts)
somaTreasuries.note: Bills ≈ $562–568bn in mid/late Oct. Substack posts quote 4,412bn and 4,573bn for late Oct. Use H.4.1 Table 1 to settle.

somaMBS.label: SOMA agency MBS
somaMBS.source: NY Fed SOMA holdings (via Apify excerpt)
somaMBS.note: Runs off ≈ $15–16bn/month. Principal is reinvested into T-bills (Dec 2025 policy).

reserves.label: Reserve balances with Federal Reserve Banks
reserves.note: Excerpts give 2.89T (H.4.1, column unclear), 2,962.6bn week-average to Oct 21, and 3,106.8bn (Substack). High-priority check.

tga.label: Treasury General Account (TGA)
tga.source: Federal Reserve H.4.1 Oct 29 2026; matches Daily Treasury Statement closing balance

reverseRepoTotal.label: Reverse repurchase agreements (all)
reverseRepoTotal.note: Nearly all of this is the foreign official reverse repo pool (foreign central banks parking dollars). The domestic ON RRP is ≈ $0.2bn.

onRrp.label: Overnight reverse repo (ON RRP) facility usage
onRrp.source: NY Fed reverse repo operations (via tftc.io excerpt)
onRrp.note: 2 counterparties, award rate 3.75%. 2026 high: $26.9bn on Jun 30 (quarter-end).

currency.label: Currency in circulation (Federal Reserve notes)
currency.source: PLACEHOLDER: last confirmed 2,416.9bn in Oct 2025 (FRED MBCURRCIR). Oct 2026 value not yet found.
currency.note: Placeholder pending H.4.1 Table 5. Do not display without the caveat.

otherLiabilitiesAndCapital.label: Other deposits, other liabilities & capital (net of deferred asset)
otherLiabilitiesAndCapital.note: Residual that forces assets = liabilities in the starting state. Includes GSE deposits and capital (~$46bn), minus the deferred asset (~$236bn), which H.4.1 books as a negative liability. Will change once reserves and currency are confirmed.

deferredAsset.label: Fed deferred asset (cumulative unremitted losses)
deferredAsset.source: Federal Reserve, Monetary Policy Report, July 2026
deferredAsset.note: Peaked above $245bn in Jan 2026 and is now shrinking slowly. Some Reserve Banks have resumed remittances (~$6bn to Treasury in 2026). CBO expects material remittances by ~2031.

qtStatus.label: Balance-sheet policy
qtStatus.value: QT ended Dec 1 2025; reserve-management bill purchases (RMPs) since Dec 12 2025
qtStatus.source: FOMC implementation notes Dec 2025; SVB, CRS IF12147
qtStatus.note: RMP pace reported as $40bn/mo from Dec 2025, then $25bn, then $10bn; one source says paused from Aug 14 2026, another says ~$10–15bn/mo. MBS principal is reinvested into bills either way. Check the latest NY Fed Desk statement.

policy_rates._note: Set by the Oct 28 2026 FOMC (hold, 10–2; two dissents favored a hike). The Sep 16 2026 meeting raised the range 25bp — the first hike since 2023 — under Chair Warsh.

ffTargetLow.label: Fed funds target range, lower bound

ffTargetHigh.label: Fed funds target range, upper bound

srfRate.label: Standing repo operations minimum bid rate (ceiling)
srfRate.note: The facility has been renamed from Standing Repo Facility (SRF) to standing repo operations (SRP).

sofr.label: SOFR
sofr.note: Oct 27 quoted as 3.91% and as 3.95%. Oct 26 = 3.90%. Either way SOFR is at or slightly above IORB, a sign reserves are near the low end of 'ample'.

market_yields._note: Treasury par yield curve / H.15, Oct 30 2026. The 3-month and 5-year values were not found and are null. The UI must show them as missing, not interpolate silently.

y3m.label: 3-month bill
y3m.note: Not found. The 3.87% average bill rate on the debt suggests a market rate near 3.8–4.0%, but do not use that as data.

y2.label: 2-year
y2.source: Treasury par yield curve (via sofrrate.com — single source)

holders._note: Who owns the debt. The building blocks come from different dates and bases, so the UI must label the denominator. Domestic private categories (mutual funds, pensions, insurers, banks, households) need the Fed's Z.1 Financial Accounts Table L.210, which has not been retrieved yet.

foreignTotal.label: Foreign holders (official + private)
foreignTotal.source: Treasury TIC, Major Foreign Holders (via secondary)
foreignTotal.note: About 41% official (central banks), 59% private. August 2026 total not found.

foreignByCountry.label: Largest foreign holders
foreignByCountry.source: Treasury TIC data for August 2026 (press release sb0662)
foreignByCountry.note: TIC records where a security is held (custody), not who ultimately owns it. UK, Belgium, Cayman and Luxembourg partly reflect custodians and hedge funds.

mmfTotalAssets.label: Money market fund total assets
mmfTotalAssets.source: ICI weekly Money Market Fund Assets
mmfTotalAssets.note: MMF holdings of Treasuries specifically (≈ half of assets?) are in the ICI/SEC N-MFP monthly holdings report — TODO.

tetherTBills.label: Tether T-bill holdings
tetherTBills.source: Tether quarterly attestation (via Motley Fool excerpt)
tetherTBills.note: Another source says ~$141bn total Treasury exposure, which probably includes reverse repo. Attestation date unconfirmed.

usdcSupply.label: USDC supply
usdcSupply.note: Most of Circle's reserves (~84% as of Jun 30) sit in the Circle Reserve Fund, a government MMF run by BlackRock.

repoMarketSize.label: US repo market, total outstanding exposures
repoMarketSize.note: Treasury repo ≈ $8.8T of this. A Sep 2026 Wolf Street piece uses $13.5T. These are outstanding positions, not daily turnover.

sofrVolume.label: SOFR underlying daily volume
sofrVolume.source: NY Fed, Teller Window: 'A Framework for Understanding the U.S. Treasury Repo Market'
sofrVolume.note: Up from ~$1T in early 2022. H1 2026 split: cleared bilateral (FICC DVP) ~$1,855bn, tri-party ~$1,280bn, GCF ~$31bn (secondary chart).

hedgeFundRepoBorrowing.label: Hedge fund repo borrowing (gross)
hedgeFundRepoBorrowing.note: All hedge-fund repo, not just basis trades. OFR estimated the basis trade itself at ~$2T at end-2025.

srfSep2026QuarterEnd.label: Standing repo take-up at Sep 30 2026 quarter-end

geniusAct.label: GENIUS Act signed
geniusAct.note: Reserves must be 1:1 in: coins and currency; demand deposits; Treasury bills, notes or bonds with ≤93 days remaining maturity; repurchase agreements (maturity ≤7 days, overnight preferred) backed by such Treasury bills; government MMFs investing only in these; central bank reserve deposits. Agencies had to finalize rules by Jul 18 2026. Effective by Jan 18 2027 at the latest (or 120 days after final rules). OCC final rule: Bulletin 2026-50 (Oct 2026).

eslr.label: eSLR reform final rule
eslr.note: Effective Apr 1 2026, with early adoption allowed from Jan 1 2026. Replaces the fixed 2% eSLR buffer for G-SIB holding companies with one tied to each bank's G-SIB surcharge (half of method 1). Frees balance sheet for dealers to hold and finance Treasuries.

jgb10y.label: Japan 10-year JGB yield
jgb10y.note: Crossed 3% on Sep 1 2026 for the first time since 1996. Peaked ≈3.12% intraday Oct 1/6. 30y record 4.235% on Oct 5.

swapLines.label: Standing dollar swap lines
swapLines.value: Bank of Canada, Bank of England, Bank of Japan, ECB, Swiss National Bank
swapLines.source: Federal Reserve, Central bank liquidity swaps

history_anchors._note: Used for the 'then vs now' notes and the future historical scrubber. All of these are from memory and must be checked.
